name: Starter: Ukrainian
about: Ukrainian word order and cases in real, everyday sentences.

words.справа: matter, thing (як справи: how are things)
words.звати: to call (мене звати: my name is)
words.подобатися: to please (мені подобається: I like it)
words.їхати: to go (by car, bus or train)
words.піти: to set off; to go (one trip)

як-справи.about: A friendly greeting: literally, how things? Answer with Добре, дякую (fine, thanks).

як-тебе-звати.about: Literally, how do they call you? Answer with Мене звати and your name.

вибачте.about: To get someone's attention, or to say sorry.

у-мене-є.about: Literally, at me there is. Without є when you describe what you have: У мене велика кімната.

дай-мені-знати.about: A fixed request: tell me, keep me posted.

concept.line: The verb's ending changes with person and number: я живу, ти живеш, він живе, ми живемо, вони живуть.
Ukrainian usually leaves out am, is and are in the present: Я студент (I'm a student); Де мої ключі?

words.means: student (male; at a university or college)

concept.line: Most nouns ending in a consonant are masculine, most in -а or -я feminine, and most in -о or -е neuter; adjectives, my and the past tense match them.
A yes/no question often keeps the order of a statement, with the voice rising (Ти говориш англійською?), or starts with чи; a question word like як, де or що often comes first in its clause.
What a verb acts on takes the accusative (кава, Я п'ю каву); so does where you're going after в or на (в магазин, на роботу) and a day (у суботу).

words.means: живе = lives; живеш = live; живу = live
йдеш = are going; йду = go; йде = goes

concept.line: To say you have something, Ukrainian often says it is at you: У мене є брат (I have a brother); describing what you have, є is left out: У мене велика кімната.
